Those who played controversial role in 1971 must apologise: Liberation War affairs minister
2026-07-11T21:00:54+06:00 | Star Online Report
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/those-who-played-controversial-role-1971-must-apologise-liberation-war-affairs-minister-4221386

Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan today urged those who played a controversial role in 1971 to accept responsibility and apologise to the nation in the interest of unity and prosperity.

Speaking at a discussion organised by the Retired Armed Forces Officers’ Welfare Association (RAOWA) in Dhaka, he said everyone must return to the spirit of the Liberation War and move beyond divisions between pro‑ and anti‑independence forces.

“We will remain united to build Bangladesh. A political party has the democratic right to hold programmes, and it is the duty of the police and administration to ensure security,” he said, adding that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called upon all to move the country forward by remaining united.

The minister stressed that those who opposed the Liberation War must come forward. “If they do not accept responsibility and apologise, it will be difficult for the nation and freedom fighters to move on. For the greater interest of the country, they must embrace democracy and the spirit of 1971,” he said.
